title: Nasi Goreng
subtitle: Indonesian fried rice with chicken and egg
excerpt: Indonesia's most famous fried rice, made with dark soy sauce, chicken, and a fried egg on top. It comes together fast and works best with rice cooked the day before.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from Indonesian home cooking traditions. Day-old rice and dark soy sauce are consistent across all major references.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook and cool the rice the day before. Spread it on a tray and refrigerate uncovered so it dries out slightly.

content.text: Day-old rice fries up better than fresh cooked rice. Get the wok very hot before anything goes in.

items.prepNote: cooked and cooled, ideally overnight in the fridge
thinly sliced, white and green parts separated

content.text: Heat 3 tablespoons of oil in the wok over very high heat until smoking. Add the chicken. Stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes until cooked through and golden. Remove and set aside.
Add 1 more tablespoon of oil. Fry the garlic, ginger, and white spring onion for 30 seconds.
Add the chilli and stir for 15 seconds. Then add the cold rice.
Press and toss the rice in the wok for 2 minutes. Break up any clumps. Drizzle over the dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, and fish sauce. Toss well.
Return the chicken to the wok. Toss everything together for 1 minute. Taste and adjust soy if needed.
In a separate pan, heat the remaining oil and fry the eggs sunny-side up until the whites are set and the edges crisp.
Divide the rice between four plates. Top each with a fried egg. Scatter over the green spring onion. Serve with cucumber slices.

items.cause: Rice was freshly cooked and too moist.
items.fix: Use day-old cold rice from the fridge.

items.symptom: Chicken is sticking to the wok.
items.cause: Wok was not hot enough before adding oil.
items.fix: Heat the wok until smoking before any oil goes in.

items.symptom: Rice looks pale and tastes bland.
items.cause: Not enough dark soy sauce for colour and depth.
items.fix: Add another tablespoon of dark soy and toss thoroughly.
